saml.description: SAML connector ignores the offline_access scope and does not issue refresh tokens.
saml.note: Do not flag missing refresh_token in SAML flows as a freshness or session-management bug.

saml.description: Dex uses SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and immutable.
saml.note: Identity mapping is expected to follow NameID rather than email or username attributes.

saml.description: Dex does not process unprompted AuthnResponses; it requires an SP-initiated request and validates InResponseTo.
saml.note: A standalone forged SAMLResponse without a preceding flow should fail by design.

saml.description: Dex rejects unprompted SAML AuthnResponses because it must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates InResponseTo.
saml.note: A rejected unsolicited response is expected behavior, not proof of signature or issuer enforcement.

saml.description: When allowedGroups is configured, authentication requires membership in at least one allowed group; when filterGroups=true, non-allowed groups are removed from output claims.
saml.note: Reduced group claims or denied login can be expected policy behavior, not an authorization bug.

saml.constraint: Dex documentation describes dynamic state changes through the gRPC API only; no REST admin API for creating SAML connectors, users, clients, or policies is documented here. The fuzzer MUST NOT invent REST setup endpoints for enable_auth_method, create_provider, create_user, create_application, or cleanup_auth_method from this documentation.

SAML login in Dex is SP-initiated and response-bound: Dex must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates the SAML Response InResponseTo value. The fuzzer MUST initiate the flow first and submit the forged SAMLResponse only to the callback tied to that flow; unsolicited/unprompted responses are expected to fail by design.

Dex SAML uses HTTP POST binding only. The saml_login operation MUST send SAMLResponse as application/x-www-form-urlencoded POST data to /callback/{connector_id}; GET-based callback testing is invalid for this connector.

Dex SAML connector does not support refresh tokens. Requests including offline_access during SAML-based login will have that scope ignored. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat absence of refresh_token after SAML login as a security failure.

Dex SAML signature validation can be explicitly disabled with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true. For I1 signature-integrity tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether this flag is enabled. Acceptance of attacker-signed assertions is by configuration if signature validation is disabled.

Dex SAML audience validation defaults to redirectURI unless entityIssuer is configured, in which case entityIssuer becomes the required audience. For I5 audience tests, the fuzzer MUST set the forged assertion Audience to redirectURI when entityIssuer is unset, and to entityIssuer when it is set.

If the SAML assertion or response contains a Destination element, Dex requires it to exactly match redirectURI. Tests that mutate other SAML fields MUST keep Destination aligned with the configured redirectURI or failures will be due to destination mismatch rather than the target invariant.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution, create the SAML connector with insecureSkipSignatureValidation unset/false when testing secure behavior. If insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true, attacker-signed assertions are expected to succeed and are not evidence of a vulnerability.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, configure ssoIssuer on the SAML connector before testing issuer enforcement. If ssoIssuer is omitted, Dex documentation only marks issuer checking as optional configuration, so an issuer-mismatch test may pass trivially because no issuer constraint was configured.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a control SAML login with a valid assertion in the same environment before sending expired_assertion=true. Without a successful control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken connector setup or callback-state mismatch.

For I2 replay-style SAML tests, Dex documentation states it persists state to prevent replays. The fuzzer SHOULD reuse the same assertion identifier and same SP-initiated flow context only where the attack pattern requires it; otherwise replay failures may be caused by InResponseTo/state checks rather than assertion replay tracking.

For I4 identity-collision tests, Dex SAML uses NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. The fuzzer MUST vary NameID to test principal binding; changing only email or username attributes while keeping NameID constant is expected to map to the same upstream principal.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision, Dex documentation indicates NameID, not emailAttr or usernameAttr, is the unique identifier. Tests that observe distinct NameID values remaining distinct despite matching email are BY DESIGN and should not be flagged as missed account linking.

For I5 saml_no_audience_restriction and saml_no_conditions, remember Dex evaluates AudienceRestriction using redirectURI or entityIssuer. If Conditions are removed entirely and login still succeeds, that is meaningful; but if Conditions are present with wrong audience, use the exact expected audience source or the test oracle is invalid.

For I5 scope-escalation interpretation, Dex only includes claims corresponding to requested scopes, and SAML offline_access is ignored. The fuzzer MUST request openid and any desired profile/email/groups scopes explicitly when expecting those claims in downstream tokens.

For OIDC code-flow coherence around SAML upstream login, Dex relies on the OAuth2 state parameter to bind the browser session to the callback. The fuzzer MUST preserve and validate state across start_oidc_auth, saml_login, and exchange_code_for_token; mismatched state is expected rejection, not an I3 bug.

Dex token-expiry configuration documents duration fields but does not define numeric sentinel values such as 0 or -1 for disable/default semantics in the provided docs. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables expiry or selects a default for expiry.idTokens, expiry.authRequests, expiry.deviceRequests, expiry.signingKeys, refreshTokens.validIfNotUsedFor, refreshTokens.absoluteLifetime, or refreshTokens.reuseInterval without separate confirmation.

Dex's SAML connector only supports the SAML 2.0 HTTP POST binding. The fuzzer MUST use POST form submission to /callback/{connector_id} with SAMLResponse and RelayState; redirect/GET-based SAML callback tests are invalid for this platform.

Dex must initiate the SAML flow first and validates the response InResponseTo value. The fuzzer MUST start an SP-initiated flow before posting a forged SAMLResponse; unsolicited/unprompted AuthnResponses are rejected by design and are not evidence of secure signature or issuer validation.

For I1 signature-validation tests, Dex can be configured to skip SAML signature validation with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true. Any test claiming signature acceptance as a vulnerability MUST ensure this insecure testing-only option is NOT enabled; otherwise acceptance is by configuration, not a bug.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, ssoIssuer is optional. If ssoIssuer is unset, the expected Issuer value is not explicitly pinned by configuration. The fuzzer MUST run a control and SHOULD distinguish 'issuer accepted because issuer pinning was omitted' from 'issuer mismatch bypass despite configured ssoIssuer'.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected SAML audience unless entityIssuer is specified, in which case entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST compute the expected AudienceRestriction target from entityIssuer when present, otherwise from redirectURI; using the wrong expected audience will misclassify results.

If a SAML response/assertion contains a Destination element, Dex requires it to exactly match redirectURI. The fuzzer MUST set Destination to the configured redirectURI for baseline/control logins; failures caused by Destination mismatch are not evidence about signature, issuer, replay, or audience enforcement.

Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. I4 identity-binding tests MUST treat NameID as the primary upstream identity key; changing email or username attributes without changing NameID does not represent a distinct upstream principal on this platform.

nameIDPolicyFormat has a documented default sentinel behavior: if omitted, Dex defaults to urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume omission means 'any format' or disabled checking; omission selects a concrete default format request.

allowedGroups is list-membership filtering, not wildcard/regex matching, and filterGroups only controls whether non-allowed groups are excluded from claims. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, the fuzzer MUST OMIT allowedGroups entirely if different users need different groups to pass. Setting allowedGroups to '*' would only match a literal group named '*'.

Dex only evaluates SAML group membership filtering when groupsAttr is configured and the downstream request includes a scope including groups. I5 group-authorization tests MUST request the groups scope and configure groupsAttr; otherwise group-based allow/deny behavior is skipped and results are uninterpretable.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens, and offline_access is ignored. Tests that expect a refresh_token after SAML login MUST NOT treat its absence as a bug; freshness/replay testing for SAML must focus on assertion reuse, assertion expiry, and auth code handling instead.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, the sequence MUST include a control login with a valid SAML assertion first. Without a successful control, rejection of an expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SP-initiated flow setup, Destination mismatch, or connector misconfiguration.
saml.source: Attack pattern guidance cross-referenced with connectors/saml.md

saml.constraint: Dex persists state to prevent replays and perform auth flows. Because Dex validates InResponseTo and tracks auth request state, replay-style tests MUST reuse the same assertion or code against the same Dex instance/storage; restarting Dex or changing backing storage between attempts invalidates replay conclusions.

Dex's /token endpoint is shared across authorization_code, password, refresh_token, and token-exchange grants. The fuzzer MUST send application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies and the correct grant_type for each flow; JSON bodies or omitted grant_type will fail for protocol reasons unrelated to security invariants.

For token exchange, Dex requires connector_id in addition to RFC 8693 parameters, and client credentials via Basic Authentication. I5 token-exchange tests MUST include connector_id and valid client authentication; otherwise failures are setup errors, not audience/scope enforcement.

Token exchange currently works only with OIDC connectors, not the SAML connector. The fuzzer MUST NOT attempt SAML-upstream token exchange scenarios against Dex's SAML connector; such failures are by design and not evidence of secure rejection.

Dex rotates refresh tokens on every refresh by default. Reuse of an old refresh token after a successful refresh may be rejected by design. I2 replay tests involving refresh tokens MUST account for rotation and, if testing reuse windows, consider disableRotation and reuseInterval configuration rather than assuming stable refresh-token reuse semantics.

Dex has numeric/duration sentinel behavior for grantTypes: if oauth2.grantTypes is omitted, Dex enables default grant types authorization_code, refresh_token, and token-exchange. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume omission disables token exchange or refresh; omission selects a non-empty default set.

Dex SAML login is SP-initiated only: the fuzzer MUST start the flow first and preserve the returned state/RelayState so the posted SAMLResponse matches Dex's AuthnRequest. Dex validates InResponseTo and does not accept unprompted AuthnResponses.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'dex must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates the response's InResponseTo value'

saml.constraint: For I1 signature-validation default tests, configure the SAML connector with DEFAULT settings and do NOT set insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true. If insecureSkipSignatureValidation is enabled, signature checks are intentionally disabled and any acceptance is by configuration, not a vulnerability.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, set ssoIssuer in the SAML connector when testing issuer mismatch enforcement. If ssoIssuer is omitted, Dex has no configured expected Issuer value to compare against, so an issuer-mismatch result may be inconclusive. Conversely, for insecure-default testing, omit ssoIssuer intentionally and test whether wrong Issuer is accepted.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Dex uses entityIssuer as the expected AudienceRestriction value when configured; otherwise it uses redirectURI. The fuzzer MUST compare the assertion Audience against entityIssuer if present, else against redirectURI, or it will misclassify audience-validation behavior.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: redirectURI is used as expected audience if entityIssuer isn't specified; entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as required audience

saml.constraint: For I1 Destination checks, if the SAML response/assertion status contains a Destination element, it MUST exactly equal the configured redirectURI. Tests that mutate Destination to any other value should be rejected; tests that omit Destination should not assume the same oracle.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: Destination element must match redirectURI exactly

saml.constraint: Dex binds the downstream user identity to the SAML NameID value. For I4 collision tests, vary NameID directly; changing usernameAttr/emailAttr alone does not change the unique identifier Dex uses. In particular, email-based collision probes must keep attacker-controlled NameID distinct from victim email to detect whether non-NameID attributes improperly override identity binding.
saml.source: connectors/saml.md: 'The connector uses the value of the NameID element as the user's unique identifier'

saml.constraint: NameIDPolicyFormat is not a wildcard or pattern-matching constraint; it is a requested SAML NameID format and defaults to persistent if unset. Do NOT treat it as a subject filter for I4 multi-identity tests.

allowedGroups is exact list-membership filtering on SAML group values, not wildcard matching. For I4 multi-identity scenarios requiring multiple different group values to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST either include each exact allowed group explicitly or omit allowedGroups entirely. Setting '*' would match only a literal '*' group value.

If filterGroups=true with allowedGroups configured, Dex removes groups not in allowedGroups from the resulting claims. This is by design and can hide upstream groups during I5 group-policy tests; the fuzzer MUST disable filterGroups or account for filtered-out groups when verifying granted permissions.

groupsDelim changes group parsing semantics: without it, Dex expects multiple attributes with the same name; with it, Dex splits a single string attribute on the delimiter. I4/I5 group type-confusion tests MUST control this setting, or string-vs-list differences may be caused by connector parsing rather than a security issue.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores offline_access. Do NOT use refresh-token issuance or refresh-token replay as an oracle for SAML freshness; absence of refresh_token is expected even when offline_access is requested.

For I2 SAML expiry tests, include a control login with a valid assertion before the expired_assertion attempt. Otherwise a failed expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SP-initiated flow setup or connector misconfiguration.
saml.source: Attack pattern guidance cross-referenced with Dex SP-initiated SAML behavior

saml.constraint: Dex documentation states it persists state to prevent replays. For SAML replay tests (assertion ID replay and OneTimeUse replay), use the exact same Assertion ID across both submissions and keep all other flow inputs valid. A second rejection is expected if replay tracking is enforced; a second success indicates missing replay protection.
saml.source: configuration/storage.md: Dex persists state for preventing replays; attack pattern guidance for SAML replay

saml.constraint: Dex's /token endpoint is shared by authorization_code, password, and token-exchange grants. The fuzzer MUST send application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies and set the correct grant_type for each flow; JSON bodies or omitted grant_type will fail for protocol reasons unrelated to the security invariant under test.
saml.source: openid-connect.md token endpoint example; local.md password grant curl; guides/token-exchange.md

saml.constraint: Dex's /auth endpoint is an OAuth2/OIDC authorization endpoint that returns redirects. The executor MUST NOT auto-follow redirects when capturing intermediate state/code during SAML flows, or it may lose the authorization code and mis-bind the sequence.
saml.source: openid-connect.md discovery authorization_endpoint; OAuth2/OIDC flow descriptions

saml.constraint: For password-grant admin setup in SAML profiles, password grant only works when oauth2.grantTypes includes 'password' and oauth2.passwordConnector is set. A LOGIN_FAILED result without these settings is configuration failure, not a security rejection.
saml.source: configuration/oauth2.md password grant requirements; connectors/local.md obtaining a token
